key_insight: A physics-based CCD noise synthesis pipeline can produce realistic, interpretable noisy astronomical images for training denoisers, overcoming the lack of paired data and improving scientific fidelity in restored images.
problem_solved: Addresses the scarcity of realistic paired clean/noisy astronomical training data and the need for reproducible, physically interpretable noise models that reflect true CCD noise formation (shot noise, dark current, readout artifacts, pixel non-uniformity).
method: Construct a modular, physics-based simulator that models successive CCD noise sources (photon shot noise, dark current, read noise, PRNU, charge transfer inefficiency) to synthesize realistic noisy images from clean inputs.
Use the synthesized paired data to train and evaluate learning-based denoisers, ensuring the simulated noise matches statistical and visual properties of real observations.
Provide reproducible pipeline components and validation metrics so trained models maintain scientific interpretability and downstream analysis fidelity.
impact: Enables AI/ML practitioners to train more effective, scientifically trustworthy denoisers for astronomical imaging using domain-accurate synthetic data, improving downstream tasks (source detection, photometry) without requiring large volumes of matched real pairs.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing sequential CCD noise sources applied to a clean image (photon → dark current → read noise → PRNU → artifacts).
Before/after denoising comparison (simulated noisy, denoised, and ground truth) highlighting preserved astronomical features.
Stacked bar or violin plots comparing statistical distributions of real vs. simulated noise components.
Flowchart linking simulator → synthetic paired dataset → denoiser training → scientific validation (e.g., photometry error plot).
paper_title: Denoising the Deep Sky: Physics-Based CCD Noise Formation for Astronomical Imaging
paper_authors: Shuhong Liu, Xining Ge, Ziying Gu, Lin Gu, Ziteng Cui
